steps.q: Does it make a great product or service?

views.text: In April 2026, Equity Mates recapped Apple’s product rollouts under its recent leadership, noting Apple Watch, AirPods, a push into services, Apple Silicon chips and Vision Pro, suggesting a broad line-up that kept users in Apple’s hardware and software ecosystem.

episode.title: End of an era at Apple, the GLP-1 surprise & top holdings of global fund managers

views.text: In September 2023, Equity Mates said investors and consumers shrugged at incremental iPhone updates, yet Apple still shipped hundreds of millions of phones annually, highlighting ongoing demand for its flagship product despite routine release cycles.

episode.title: Apple’s new iPhone - Does anyone care?

views.text: In March 2023, Equity Mates outlined reporting that Apple had worked for years on non‑invasive glucose monitoring for Apple Watch, arguing it could change life for diabetics and strengthen the watch’s appeal if the technology proved successful.

episode.title: Apple's top secret healthcare startup has been revealed

steps.q: Will it keep earning above market profits?

views.text: In October 2023, Equity Mates covered the Epic Games dispute, noting a US court decision that Epic had not shown Apple had monopoly power, while related Australian cases continued, underscoring ongoing scrutiny of Apple’s market power.

episode.title: What’s the latest in the Epic Games v Apple stoush?

views.text: In September 2023, Equity Mates discussed user stickiness, sharing that switching away from iPhone led to missing iMessage group chats before returning, illustrating how Apple’s ecosystem created friction to leave.

episode.title: Apple’s new iPhone - Does anyone care?

views.text: In December 2022, Equity Mates explained how Apple controlled the iOS ecosystem via the App Store, including a 30% fee and privacy changes, and described complaints from rivals who argued Apple competed while also running the platform.

episode.title: The controversy over Apple's App Store explained

steps.q: Can it reinvest its profits productively?

views.text: In April 2026, Equity Mates noted Apple invested in services and vertically integrated with Apple Silicon, indicating reinvestment to improve margins and control key technology.

episode.title: End of an era at Apple, the GLP-1 surprise & top holdings of global fund managers

views.text: In May 2024, Equity Mates highlighted Apple’s US$110 billion share buyback, describing how reducing share count returned capital to shareholders and set a new record, following Apple’s previous largest buyback.

episode.title: Highlights from Berkshire Hathaway, Apple’s record buyback & crypto’s record price

views.text: In June 2023, Equity Mates discussed Apple’s launch of Vision Pro and weighed its potential as the next step in computing, reflecting ongoing investment in new product categories.

episode.title: Apple’s Vision 👓 + can Bryce find bargains in the dog kennel?

steps.q: Can it be bought at a reasonable price?

views.text: In April 2026, Equity Mates contrasted strong long‑term shareholder returns with recent debates over Apple’s AI approach and product innovation, implying differing views on what future growth was priced into the stock.

episode.title: End of an era at Apple, the GLP-1 surprise & top holdings of global fund managers

views.text: In May 2024, Equity Mates noted Apple’s shares hadn’t matched some tech peers despite huge profits, saying markets were forward‑looking, with long‑running concerns about iPhone sales tempered by the rise of services.

episode.title: Highlights from Berkshire Hathaway, Apple’s record buyback & crypto’s record price

views.text: In February 2023, Equity Mates worked through valuing Apple, saying it was so well covered that mispricings were rare and that a variant perception was needed, with recent model tweaks driven by slowing services growth and disclosed subscriber metrics.

episode.title: How to value a company: Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) Pt. 3
